slides.title: Strep: common at 5–10 and 15–25 yrs, rare <3 yrs
Viral in 70–90% of cases; bacterial ~10–30%

nodes.label: Viral 70–90% of cases
nodes.text: Cough; pharyngeal inflammation, ulcer ± exudate; fever, headache.
nodes.src: Viral 70–90% of cases: 1 cough; 2 pharyngeal inflammation ulcer ± exudate; 3 fever, headache.

nodes.label: Bacterial ~10–30%
nodes.text: Absence of cough; tonsillar exudate; fever, tender cervical lymph nodes.
nodes.sub: Most common: Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus (S. pyogenes).
nodes.src: Bacterial ~10–30% (most common: Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus / S. pyogenes): 1 absence of cough; 2 Tonsillar exudate; 3 fever, tender cervical lymph nodes.

slides.title: Bacterial: sudden, severe, fever >38, no cough
head: Viral
Bacterial
rows: 7–10 days, needs antibiotics if strep confirmed
src: ONSET: Viral More gradual; Bacterial Sudden.
Throat pain: Viral Mild to moderate; Bacterial severe.
Cough, coryza, rhinorrhea: Viral Common; Bacterial absent.
Tonsils: Viral Red, swollen, little/no exudate; Bacterial Enlarged, purulent exudates.
Lymph nodes: Viral Mild or absent; Bacterial Tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy.
Duration: Viral 5–7 days, self-limiting; Bacterial 7–10 days, needs antibiotics if strep confirmed.
Systemic: Viral Malaise, fatigue, conjunctivitis; Bacterial Headache, abdominal pain (children).

slides.title: Management: nonpharmacological, pharmacological, tonsillectomy

nodes.label: 1 NonPharmacological
nodes.text: Hydration, warm saline gargles, soft diet

nodes.text: Analgesics, topical anesthetics, NSAID lozenges, antibiotics

slides.title: Tonsillectomy: ≥7 episodes in 1 year
Penicillin V first-line; avoid amoxicillin if EBV

mcq.q: A 16-year-old male adolescent suffers from recurrent tonsillitis more than 7 times over the past year, with difficulty swallowing and snoring during sleep. What is the most appropriate management?
mcq.why: ≥7 episodes in 1 year is an indication for tonsillectomy.

mcq.q: A child 4 years old has sore throat. Which medication is suitable for this case?
mcq.why: Benzocaine lozenge >3 yrs; Lidocaine and Flurbiprofen >12 years.

mcq.q: An 8-year-old girl complained of a sore throat for two days, no cough, a fever of 38.5°C, and enlarged anterior cervical lymph nodes. What is the most appropriate treatment?
mcq.why: Penicillin V is first-line: a 10-day course.

mcq.q: For the same girl, what is the appropriate pharmacist advice?
opts: Take antibiotics only until symptoms subside
Complete the full course of antibiotics
Use benzydamine nasal spray for children under 3 years of age
mcq.why: Complete the full course: Penicillin V is a 10-day course.

mcq.q: Which antibiotic is used in glandular fever (EBV)?
mcq.why: Avoid amoxicillin (Augmentin) if EBV glandular fever is suspected.
mcq.src: Avoid if EBV Glandular fever (EBV) fever, malaise, rash, splenomegaly suspected (rash).

mcq.q: A woman in the eighth month of pregnancy is complaining of a mild sore throat, without fever. What is the safe option to relieve the symptoms?
mcq.why: Lidocaine is not safe in pregnancy; flurbiprofen: avoid in 3rd trimester.
mcq.src: Pregnancy (page 12): Flurbiprofen → avoid in 3trimester) pregnancy. Lidocaine → Not safe.
